sentenceSets.sentence: The funds were misappropriated over a period of years, in amounts too small to trigger automatic scrutiny.

answerChoices.reasoning: Embezzlement requires that the taker held the money in trust as part of his office, a relationship the sentence never establishes about whoever moved these sums.
Squandering is wasteful spending on the intended holder's own account, which would show up as loss rather than as sums kept small enough to slip past the thresholds.
Diverting only says the money went somewhere other than planned, which can be a lawful reallocation, whereas the deliberate sizing of the amounts to avoid scrutiny points to wrongful taking.
Laundering disguises the origin of money already obtained illegally, but the sentence describes the taking itself, with concealment achieved simply by keeping each amount below the review threshold.
Auditing is the very scrutiny the small amounts were designed to escape, so it cannot also be what was done to the funds.
Depreciation is an accounting write-down of an asset's value over time, an ordinary and disclosed process rather than something structured to avoid detection.
Reimbursement returns money to someone who spent it, which would not need to be hidden beneath a scrutiny threshold.
Freezing funds blocks their movement, whereas here the money moved repeatedly in carefully sized increments.
Donating is an open transfer for charitable purposes and would not be arranged to avoid automatic review.
Replenishing adds money back to an account, the opposite of what happened to these funds.
Publicizing draws attention, contradicting a scheme built on keeping each amount beneath notice.

sentenceSets.sentence: The council treasurer resigned after admitting he had misappropriated the flood relief account to cover the shortfall in his own building firm.

answerChoices.reasoning: Plundering suggests violent seizure by an outsider, but this man held the account as treasurer and moved the money quietly enough that only his own admission brought it out.
Pilfering means taking small items of little value, which cannot describe drawing on a relief account to cover a company's shortfall.
Mismanagement is incompetent handling with no personal gain, whereas the money went to his own firm and cost him his post.
Borrowing presumes permission and an arrangement to repay, neither of which fits a treasurer who had to resign as soon as he admitted what he had done.
Forfeiting is losing something as a penalty, but here the treasurer gained the use of the money rather than surrendering anything.
Disclosure is the admission that came afterward, not the act with the account that forced him out of office.
Investing places money to earn a return for the fund's owner, whereas this money plugged a hole in his private business.
Insuring protects an account against loss, which would be a defensible act rather than a resigning offence.
Replenishing the relief account would have been the remedy, not the admission that ended his career.
Inheriting comes by bequest and would give him lawful title, contradicting the resignation.
Commending is praising and cannot be done to a flood relief account.

sentenceSets.sentence: Artists in the collective accused the fashion house of misappropriating their designs, reproducing the motifs on scarves without payment or acknowledgment.

answerChoices.reasoning: Plagiarism is passing another's work off as one's own original creation, but the complaint here rests on commercial reproduction without payment, which is possible even where the source is admitted.
Imitation produces something in a similar manner, whereas the sentence says the motifs themselves were reproduced on the scarves.
Licensing is the lawful purchase of permission to use a design, which is precisely what the missing payment and acknowledgment show did not happen.
Adapting reworks material for a new medium and is generally treated as creative labour, but the artists object to the taking itself rather than to any transformation.
Cataloguing lists and records works, an archival act that would not put the motifs onto merchandise for sale.
Exhibiting displays the artists' work as theirs, which would supply exactly the acknowledgment the sentence says was withheld.
Critiquing evaluates the designs in words and would produce no scarves at all.
Commissioning would mean the house had engaged and paid the artists, contradicting the absence of payment at the heart of the accusation.
Crediting is the acknowledgment the artists say they never received.
Discarding throws the designs away, which cannot produce scarves carrying the motifs.
Insulating shields something from heat or influence and has no bearing on the reuse of designs.
